skill.name: managing-project-rules
skill.description: Creates and updates focused Claude Code rule files in .claude/rules, including scoped rules, naming guidance, and organization patterns.
skill.summary: Helps teams create focused, scoped Claude Code project rules.
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: Review confirmed high-risk guidance for symlinks and user-level ~/.claude/rules, which can load instructions from outside the repository and persist across projects. The SKILL.md backtick and YAML frontmatter hits are false positives because they are prose references, not executable commands or reconnaissance. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: User-level rule writes can persist across projects.
remediation.suggestion: State that the skill must not create or edit ~/.claude/rules unless the user explicitly requests global rules and approves the exact path.

remediation.issue: Symlink examples can load rule content from outside the repository.
remediation.suggestion: Remove symlink creation examples or require explicit user confirmation and target review before creating symlinks into .claude/rules.

remediation.issue: Default scope could be clearer for project-boundary safety.
remediation.suggestion: Make current-repository .claude/rules the default scope and summarize every created or modified rule file after changes.

finding_verdicts.reason: The reference describes creating rules in ~/.claude/rules that apply across projects, which can persist AI behavior outside the current workspace. This is documentation rather than direct execution, so confidence is high but not absolute.
The listed ~/.claude/rules path is a hidden home-directory location used for global rule loading. Editing it can affect future sessions and projects beyond the user-visible project scope.

The guidance points to ~/.claude/rules as a place for personal rules, which is hidden filesystem access with cross-project impact. It is legitimate Claude configuration but still a real persistence risk.

The explicit ~/.claude/rules directory reference can lead an agent to inspect or modify hidden user-level configuration. The risk is contextual but real because those files influence future Claude behavior.
The ln -s example links a home-directory rules folder into .claude/rules. That can cause rule loading from outside the repository and can bypass normal project-boundary review.
The command links an external home-directory file into project rules, making outside content part of Claude memory. This can unexpectedly load sensitive or unreviewed instructions.
Line 6 uses Markdown backticks around .claude/rules in prose. There is no Ruby code, shell evaluation, or executable command on this line.
Line 14 uses Markdown backticks to identify a local documentation path. It instructs reading a reference file and does not execute shell code.
Line 15 uses Markdown backticks around a directory name in a workflow bullet. It describes analysis of project files and does not contain command execution.
Line 30 uses Markdown backticks around the target rules directory. It describes file creation or update behavior, not Ruby backtick execution.
Line 45 uses Markdown backticks for a directory path in acceptance criteria. No executable shell command or interpreter call is present.
Validating YAML frontmatter syntax is normal documentation hygiene, not host enumeration. The line does not request system information or reconnaissance commands.

content.value_statement: Teams often let AI project instructions grow into one hard-to-maintain file. This skill helps create focused Claude Code rule files with scoped paths, clear names, and update steps.
actual_capabilities: Reads the included .claude/rules reference documentation before planning changes.
Reviews existing project rule files to preserve structure and avoid duplicates.
Creates or updates focused Markdown rule files in .claude/rules.
Adds YAML frontmatter for path-specific rules when needed.
Recommends descriptive kebab-case filenames and topic-based organization.
Reports the changed rule location, scope, and summary after completion.
limitations: It is written for Claude Code rule files and may not fit other AI memory systems.
It does not validate rule behavior by running Claude Code after edits.
It should not edit global ~/.claude/rules without explicit user approval.
It relies on user review for rule content accuracy and policy decisions.

use_cases.title: Create Team Coding Standards
use_cases.description: Turn scattered team preferences into focused rule files for style, testing, security, and review expectations.

use_cases.title: Scope Rules To File Paths
use_cases.description: Add frontmatter so API, frontend, or test rules apply only when Claude Code works in matching paths.

use_cases.title: Refine Existing Rule Sets
use_cases.description: Update existing .claude/rules files while preserving useful sections, removing duplicates, and improving filenames.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Basic Rule
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one new rule file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code project rule for our testing expectations. Keep it focused, use a descriptive filename, and place it in .claude/rules.

prompt_templates.title: Update Existing Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve current rules without losing useful content.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing .claude/rules files and update the coding style guidance. Preserve useful content, remove duplicates, and summarize every change.

prompt_templates.title: Add Path-Specific Guidance
prompt_templates.scenario: Create conditional rules for part of a repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create path-specific Claude Code rules for files under src/api. Include frontmatter, API validation expectations, and a concise completion summary.

prompt_templates.title: Restructure A Rule Library
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit our .claude/rules directory, propose a topic-based structure, then update the files after approval. Keep one topic per file and avoid global rule changes.

output_examples.input: Create testing rules for this repository.
output_examples.output: A focused testing rule file is added under .claude/rules with expectations for test naming, coverage, fixtures, and completion checks.

output_examples.input: Make frontend rules apply only to React components.
output_examples.output: A path-scoped frontend rule is created with frontmatter for component files and concise guidance for props, styling, and accessibility.
The rule directory is reviewed, duplicate guidance is consolidated, filenames are normalized, and a summary lists each changed file.

best_practices: Keep each rule file focused on one topic with a descriptive kebab-case filename.
Use path-specific frontmatter only when the rule truly applies to limited files.
Review proposed changes before editing global or shared Claude rule locations.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated style, testing, security, and workflow rules in one large file.
Do not create symlinks to external rule files without clear approval and target review.
Do not edit ~/.claude/rules when the user asked only for project-level rules.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates or updates Markdown rule files in .claude/rules for Claude Code project memory.

faq.question: Can it update existing rule files?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to preserve useful structure, remove duplicates, and report the changes made.

faq.question: Does it support path-specific rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It can add YAML frontmatter with path patterns when rules should apply only to certain files.

faq.question: Should it edit global Claude rules?
faq.answer: Only with explicit approval. Global ~/.claude/rules can affect every project, so project rules should be the default.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: The skill instructions focus on reading and editing rule files. The included reference contains symlink examples that need caution.

faq.question: Who is this for?
faq.answer: It is for teams and maintainers who want structured Claude Code instructions in a repository.
